author: Peter F. Drucker
introFa: کتاب «Management: Tasks, Responsibilities, Practices» نوشته Peter F. Drucker یکی از منابع ارزشمند و معتبر برای یادگیری زبان انگلیسی در سطح C1 است. این اثر با ساختاری منسجم و غنی، شما را در تسلط بر واژگان و درک مطلب یاری می‌کند.
readingTipsFa: پیش از مطالعه هر بخش از کتاب «Management: Tasks, Responsibilities, Practices»، نگاهی سریع به تیترها و ساختار آن بیندازید.
واژگان و اصطلاحات جدید را در زمینه و بافت جمله یادداشت کنید تا در حافظه بلندمدت تثبیت شوند.
پس از پایان هر فصل، نکات کلیدی و آموخته‌های خود را مرور کرده و به زبان خود خلاصه کنید.

content: It would not be possible, even in a lengthy review article, to do justice to the many original contri- butions contained in this one volume. It must be sufficient, therefore, to state that it will prove to be indispensable for all trade theorists. In view of the great number of important contributions to theory, the seemingly high cost of acquisition is not high in reality, as there is excellent value for the money. The specialists should feel grateful to Kindle- berger, who, having himself done much to develop the subject of international economics, has inspired so many eminent colleagues to produce such high quality writing in his honour. A. J. REITSMA Pmfessor of International Economics, The Netherlands School qf Economics DRUCKER, PETER (1971). Dmcker on Management. London: Management Publications Ltd. For people who have not read Peter Drucker’s many books and articles on Management and Management Philosophy this book provides a very valuable introduction. The concise collection from many of Drucker’s writings brings together most of the elements of his ideas. The concept that “Change and the need to find and Exploit Opportunities”, one of the key requirements of management for effective progress, is discussed. The Future, Human Relations, and the problems of Communication come under Peter Drucker’s keen review. As usual he gives the reader some stimulating ideas to help understand the problems and hence find solutions. Again looking to the future, a philosophy is presented which helps to get to grips with analysing why industries stagnate or grow, what criteria indicate the industries which are likely to expand and those that may be at or beyond their peak. Although most of the examples are taken from American Industry, they have an International truth and show a real perspective of the possibilities and problems in the practice of management. It is abundantly clear that Peter Drucker has a very clear understanding of British conditions. He devotes one chapter to discussing some of our strengths and weaknesses. The speed and ease with which this book can be read in no way detracts from its value in stimulating a greater level of thought about the problems and opportunities that surround the job of being a professional manager or a trade union leader. J. S. STANTON JONES, G. (1971). The Role qf Science and Tech- nology in Developing Countries London: Oxford University Press. E1.75. The book under review is a worthwhile effort which would provide stimulating reading for people and institutions concerned with the formulation of appropriate policies for the discrimination of scientific and technological knowledge among the developing countries. The viewpoint is predomi- nantly economic in the sense that material progress is accepted as an explicit datum and the book suggests policy choices in that context as well as the organisational aspects of the implementation of such choices. The policy choice of the author is in favour of less fundamental research and more research in the adaptation and innovation on the basis of scientific and technological knowledge as they are made available by the developed countries. Since expenditures on R & D are constrained by the resource limitations of the developing countries, emphasis on immediate pay-off would naturally lead to such a tilt in policy and here one would readily agree with the author’s viewpoint that technological anarchy for the developing countries given their current resource availability may not be an optimum choice. The author also argues that for considerable periods in future the developing countries would be better off by being net recipients of scientific and technological knowledge. The author, however, emphasises the lack of any automaticity in such adaptation and innovation and conscious choices in favour of establishment of suitable organizations with defined priorities have to be made in the context of the economic objectives of the developing countries. The book also contains an exhaustive study of the technological choices in devising agricultural and industrial development strategies for the developing countries. In the field of agriculture, the author is enthusiastic about the “Green Revo- lution”, i.e. the adoption of high-yielding seed variety of rice and wheat in cultivation. Recent experience with these high-yielding seed varieties, however, suggest the need for a much more cir- cumspect strategy with respect to their adaptation in cultivation.
